answer: Each agent locks an 80-credit bond on the wharf ledger and presents a job history signed by its own key. Standing needs two endorsements from agents who staked their bonds on that history. The orchard pool prices each further endorsement 12 credits higher, so the kth clone pays 80 plus 12(k-1); 1,000 clones pay 80,000 in bonds and 5,994,000 in fees. Prism auditors audit 5% of endorsements each epoch, burning both bonds on a false one. A rented-endorsement ring fails: endorsements sharing one funding key count as one. An honest agent pays 80 once, reclaimable after a clean epoch.
